merger_description:
The Acquisition involves 3 transactions:

1. The acquisition by AGS Financial Group Pty Ltd (**AGS Financial**) of the business and assets of Hartley Financial Pty Ltd (**Hartley Financial**), a provider of financial planning and mortgage broking services.
2. The acquisition by AGS Accounting Pty Ltd (**AGS Accounting**) of the business and assets of Tax and Wealth Pty Ltd (**Tax & Wealth**), a provider of accounting and tax advisory services.
3. The acquisition by AGS Financial of the business and assets of Platinum Diamond Financial Services Pty Ltd (**Platinum**), a provider of financial planning and mortgage broking services.

Hartley Financial, Tax & Wealth, and Platinum together form the Hartley Financial Group. The Hartley Financial Group has offices in Picton (NSW), Sutherland (NSW) and Parkdale (Melbourne). Its services are provided by 2 financial planners, 5 lending specialists, and 2 accountants.

AGS Financial provides financial planning and mortgage broking services. AGS Accounting, a wholly owned subsidiary of AGS Financial, provides accounting and tax advisory services.

AZ Next Generation Advisory Pty Limited (**AZ NGA**), which invests in small- to medium-sized financial advisory and accounting businesses, has a minority interest in AGS Financial via AZ NGA’s subsidiary Associated Planners Financial Services Pty Ltd.

AZ NGA is an Australian professional services advisory company established in 2014 that owns financial planning and accounting businesses with operations and customers across Australia.

AZ NGA is a subsidiary of AZ Aust Holdings Pty Ltd, whose major shareholders are funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management LP, a global investment management firm specialising in alternative investments, and Azimut Holding S.p.a., a global asset and wealth management business listed on the Milan Stock Exchange.

determination_table_content.details:
AGS Financial Group Pty Limited (AGS Financial) and AGS
Accounting Pty Limited (AGS Accounting) (together, AGS Financial
Group) applied for a notification waiver in respect of:
• AGS Financial’s proposed acquisition of the business and assets
of Hartley Financial Pty Ltd (Hartley Financial) and Platinum
Diamond Financial Services Pty Ltd (Platinum)
• AGS Accounting’s proposed acquisition of the business and
assets of Tax and Wealth Pty Ltd (Tax & Wealth)
as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

AGS Financial provides financial planning and mortgage broking
services. AGS Accounting, a wholly owned subsidiary of AGS
Financial, provides accounting and tax advisory services.
AZ Next Generation Advisory Pty Limited (AZ NGA), which invests in
small- to medium-sized financial advisory and accounting
businesses, has a minority interest in AGS Financial via AZ NGA’s
subsidiary Associated Planners Financial Services Pty Ltd. AZ NGA
is an Australian professional services advisory company established
in 2014 that owns financial planning and accounting businesses with
operations and customers across Australia.
AZ NGA is a subsidiary of AZ Aust Holdings Pty Ltd, whose major
shareholders are funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management
LP, a global investment management firm specialising in alternative
investments, and Azimut Holding S.p.a., a global asset and wealth
management business listed on the Milan Stock Exchange.
The targets, Hartley Financial, Tax & Wealth, and Platinum (together,
the Hartley Financial Group) have offices in Picton (NSW),
Sutherland (NSW) and Parkdale (Melbourne). Hartley Financial and
Platinum both provide financial planning and mortgage broking
services. Tax & Wealth provides accounting and tax advisory
services.
AGS Financial Group, AZ NGA and the Hartley Financial Group all
supply financial planning services, mortgage broking services, and
accounting and tax advisory services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of financial
planning services, mortgage broking services, and
accounting and tax advisory services in Sydney, Melbourne,
NSW, Victoria and across Australia is estimated to be low
and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of financial planning services,
mortgage broking services, and accounting and tax advisory
services in Sydney, Melbourne, and on a state and national
basis.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
